q: Conditional entropy H(X|Y) satisfies the chain rule H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X). The non-negativity of mutual information I(X;Y) = H(X) − H(X|Y) ≥ 0 means:
opts: Conditioning never increases entropy: H(X|Y) ≤ H(X)
Conditioning on Y makes X deterministic
exp: H(X|Y) ≤ H(X): knowledge of Y can only decrease (or maintain) uncertainty about X. Equality holds iff X ⊥ Y (independent). This is equivalent to I(X;Y) ≥ 0 (non-negativity of mutual information, which follows from non-negativity of KL divergence).
